**Type:** Story | Task · **Epic:** <!-- epic --> · **Estimate:** <!-- n -->h · **Depends on:** <!-- ticket titles or — -->

## Goal

<!-- What hurts in the business today and what this change removes, in 3-6 lines. Business words only:
     no API name, no object or field in backticks. -->

## User / Business Requirement

<!-- Story only; delete this section on a Task.
     As a <persona>, when <situation>, I need <capability>, so that <benefit>. -->

## Solution summary

<!-- What the system does, in business language, with the field labels users see.
     **Preconditions.** only when there are any; then the behaviour as short prose.
     On a Task: the end state the developer reaches. -->

### Business Rules

<!-- Bullets grouped under bold topic headings (**Availability**, **Limits**, ...), one rule per bullet.
     Include what the system deliberately does not do and what it assumes. A Story always has Business Rules.
     A text the system shows is given exactly, in double quotes. -->

## Salesforce context

<!-- Whenever the ticket names any metadata; delete otherwise. Grouped by kind under bold words
     (**Object**, **Flow**, **Access**, **Repository**, ...). Field tables: Label | API name | Type | Notes.
     Every API name the ticket uses appears here. -->

## Security

<!-- Only when the ticket touches secrets or personal data; delete otherwise. -->

## Acceptance criteria

<!-- Numbered AC1, AC2, ... One behaviour per criterion, exactly one action in When. No checkboxes.
     Numbers never change after the ticket is published: strike a removed criterion through, add new ones at the end. -->

**AC1 — title**
- **Given** …
- **When** …
- **Then** …

<!-- What a reader could wrongly assume is included, and where it belongs. -->
